subtitle: An interactive investigation into causal inference, language model decision-making, and experimental validity.
headline: When evidence changes, does the model change its mind?

research_at_a_glance.title: Original Hypothesis
research_at_a_glance.summary: Does aggressive post-training quantization increase an AI agent's reliance on misleading observational associations when choosing causal interventions, beyond general task degradation?

research_at_a_glance.title: Causal Evaluation Problem
research_at_a_glance.summary: Early pilots (Cohorts 001–007) revealed that 3B/7B F16 references failed baseline competence, emitted Markdown-fenced JSON, collapsed at Q2_K, or decoupled numeric estimates from explicit actions.

research_at_a_glance.title: Methodological Discoveries
research_at_a_glance.summary: Cohort 016 confirmed a +62.5 pp evidence-order shift in 7B Q4_K_M, but retrospective auditing found a source-blind smaller-gap heuristic solved 768/768 items. Cohorts 018–028 uncovered option-position policies, token-mapping sensitivity, and arithmetic bottlenecks.

research_at_a_glance.title: Final Controlled Experiment (CF-TP1)
research_at_a_glance.summary: Cohort 029 constructed 128 independent numerical families where identical printed tables admit opposite randomized vs. historical provenance assignments, crossed with two target-population mixtures.

research_at_a_glance.title: Scientific Contribution
research_at_a_glance.summary: On Qwen2.5-7B Q4_K_M, causal fidelity (25.00%) and arithmetic fidelity (28.52%) differed by -3.52 pp (95% t CI [-7.77, +0.74], inconclusive). Directional scoring exposed 995/1,024 causal activation bias (3/256 reversals) vs. 45/256 unwarranted arithmetic flips.

established: CF-TP1 breaks source-blind magnitude and constant-action shortcuts while achieving 4,096/4,096 strict-valid responses and 50/50 release verification checks.
In Cohort 029, Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct Q4_K_M exhibited a near-constant causal activation preference (995/1,024) and solved only 3/256 required causal target-switch pairs.
In Cohort 016, physical presentation order shifted 7B Q4_K_M conflict accuracy by +62.5 pp (95% t CI [+56.6, +68.4], t(95)=21.10, p=1.24e-37) across 96 fresh families.
Across Cohorts 020–024, Qwen 7B F16 identified the governing randomized study (up to 128/128) yet still scored near chance (43–45%) on two-source action decisions.
In Cohort 028, deterministic calculator assistance rescued noncausal controls (to 87.5–100%) but failed to rescue causal graph-to-rule selection (~50%).
unresolved: Primary Cohort 029 causal-minus-arithmetic contrast (-3.52 pp, 95% t CI [-7.77, +0.74]) spans zero; neither causal-specific impairment nor equivalence is established.
Selective causal reasoning degradation under post-training quantization remains unestablished across all 29 cohorts (no F16 arm in Cohort 029; heterogeneous/non-monotone patterns in Cohort 024).
Internal neural causal representations or attention circuits cannot be identified from behavioral binary choices without mechanistic interventions.
Generalization of CF-TP1 findings to other model families, larger scales, unquantized F16, or multi-turn tool-using agents remains open.

provenance.definition: Cohort 029 CF-TP1 primary target-pair fidelity and repository-wide inventory counts
provenance.ci_method: Stratified Welch-Satterthwaite 95% t CI & Hoeffding bounded CI
provenance.statistical_test: Paired within-family difference across 8 design strata
provenance.limitations: Single quantized deployment (Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct Q4_K_M); no F16 comparison arm in Cohort 029; primary CI crosses zero.
